messages:
alex: Heads up — seeing a spike of backfills on the eu-west dedicated GPU pool since ~02:12 UTC. Small jobs are being scheduled onto freshly provisioned spot nodes and then preempted when large gang jobs land. :grimacing:
priya: @alex can you paste an example event/log? sounds like affinity + backfill mismatch
alex: quick events from a failing pod:
```
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age    From               Message
  ----    ------     ----   ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled  2m     default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/train-worker-42 to ip-10-1-2-3.eu-west1b
  Warning BackOff    1m     kubelet            Back-off restarting failed container
  Warning Preempted  30s    kube-scheduler     Preempted by higher priority pod default/gang-train-01
```
Also seeing `0/50 nodes are available: 50 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` interleaved with preemptions.
sam: Are those small pods annotated with the soft AZ affinity? We added that to reduce cross-AZ egress a while back
alex: yes — many have `redwood/soft-az-affinity: prefer-same-az` and use `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` with weight 100
jordan: That is the crux — preferredDuringScheduling is advisory. Under pressure scheduler will place pods anywhere, then gang jobs that expect co-located GPUs land and preempt the ad-hoc pods. The observed pattern: small pods get scattered -> gang arrives -> gang preempts -> small pods bounce -> backfill churn.
lee: autoscaler-bot: `Scaled up 3 gpu nodes in eu-west1b (reason: pending pods)` :eyes:
priya: Two obvious mitigations: 1) make gang leader use required affinity to pin to AZ (but we hate hard AZ locks for multi-tenant infra), or 2) change the placement heuristics so backfill scheduling prefers AZ-local packing when GPU utilization < X, avoiding cross-AZ scattering.
sam: Another option: add a scheduling filter that prevents backfill pods with `soft-az-affinity` from being scheduled in an AZ that already has >= Y% of reserved ganged capacity for the next Xs, i.e., leave room for gangs. Could be implemented as a scheduler plugin (predicate) or as an extender.
alex: quick patch I tested locally — `kubectl patch` to lower the weight on preferred affinity to 10 for the noisy job queue, which reduced cross-AZ placement in the replay. Example patch we used in test cluster:
```
kubectl patch deployment noisy-backfill -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood/soft-az-weight":"10"}}}}}'
```
That dropped cross-AZ placements by ~60% in my sim.
jordan: Good data point. But short term we should: A) throttle aggressive backfills (reduce parallelism), B) add a soft holdback so autoscaler doesn't instantly spread across AZs, C) schedule a follow-up to implement a scheduling plugin that is AZ-aware for GPU backfills.
lee: Ops cost note — this churn equals ~120 GPU-hours wasted over the last 6h (~$720 at our book rate). If we don't act this will compound during EU traffic peaks.
priya: I'll open a quick rollback/mitigation PR: 1) lower soft affinity weight for `backfill.*` labels, 2) set `maxParallelism` on our backfill controller to 8, 3) add a temporary admission webhook to tag backfill pods with `redwood/pack-hint: prefer-same-az`.
sam: For the longer term I volunteer to prototype a scheduler plugin 'gpu-backfill-controller' that considers gang reservations and leaves slack capacity per AZ. It would run as a filter + score plugin.
alex: Thanks. Can someone own the incident alert tweak? Right now alarms trigger on overall pending pods — we should split metrics so we alert when cross-az scattering ratio > 0.3.
jordan: I'll take alerting + follow-up doc for tradeoffs (cost vs anti-affinity).
lee: I'll add a watch on the billing dashboard and mute autoscaler aggressive policies for eu-west until mitigations land.
priya: PR link (draft): https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/4523 — contains the emergency patches and a runbook note.
alex: Great. TL;DR: root cause = high-weight soft AZ affinity + aggressive backfill parallelism + autoscaler spreading -> leads to scatter/backfill/preempt cycle. Short fixes rolling, midterm plugin, longterm scheduler change.
jordan: I'll schedule a 30min sync after the PR lands to validate with synthetic gang load. :white_check_mark:
autoscaler-bot: `Notice: temporarily reduced cross-az spread factor from 1.0 -> 0.6 in eu-west`
lee: monitoring: set a 2h post-deploy watch window and reconvene if wasted GPU-hours > 50 in that window
priya: Thanks team — tagging @oncall for visibility.
